title: Optimized protocol for isolation of high-quality single cells from the female mouse reproductive tract tissues for single-cell RNA sequencing
protocol: Euthanize experimental mice using the appropriate ethically approved technique.
Sterilize the mouse by spraying with 70% ethanol on the whole-body surface.
Firmly immobilize the euthanized mouse on the dissection platform, with the ventral side facing up.
Make an incision in the skin and underlying abdominal muscles extending down to the genital part using sterile scissors.
Clear off any connective tissue from the FRT.
Using bent forceps, carefully lift out the entire genital tissue by holding at the middle part of the cervix region.
Cut out the tissue from the area connected to the vagina.
Place the FRT tissue in an empty 100 mm Petri dish.
Remove any associated adipose and connective tissue.
Transfer the tissue to a 15 mL Falcon tube containing 10 mL ice-cold PBS.
Wash tissue by inverting the tube several times.
Transfer the tissue to a sterile 100 mm Petri dish using forceps.
Separate ectocervix based on its hard, dense, and fibrous texture and proximity to the vagina.
Cut the vaginal region from the ectocervix.
Choose a region close to the place of uterine horns bifurcation for dissecting endocervical tissue.
Dissect out an area overlapping with defined ectocervix and endocervix, called the transition zone (TZ).
Place different FRT tissue regions in separate 100 mm Petri dishes.
Use a separate scalpel blade to cut the ectocervix and endocervix region from the cervix junction to avoid contamination of cells between tissues.
Mince uterine cervix tissue into small pieces using sterile scissors (less than 0.5 mm³ thickness).
Maintain single-cell suspensions in a cool condition to ensure high-quality RNA for sequencing.
Prepare single-cell suspensions within a short time after dissection.
Hold tissue with forceps during mincing.
Mince cervix tissue into small pieces with scissors and a scalpel blade.
Transfer minced tissue to a 15 mL Falcon tube containing 3 mL of pre-warmed collagenase type II (0.5 mg/mL).
Incubate tubes at 37°C for 45 minutes, shaking at 180 rpm in a horizontal position.
Seal the cap of the Falcon tube with Parafilm to prevent leakage and loss of cells during incubation.
Gently pipette up and down 20 times after digestion to dissociate cell aggregates.
Centrifuge the suspension at 1000 × g for 6 minutes at 4°C.
Discard the supernatant carefully, retaining the pellet.
Add 3 mL of pre-warmed TrypLE to the cell pellet.
Resuspend the cell pellet using a 5 mL pipette by pipetting up and down five times.
Incubate in a shaking incubator at 180 rpm for 15 minutes at 37°C.
Seal the Falcon tube cap with Parafilm to prevent leakage.
Gently pipette up and down 20 times with a 1 mL pipette to dissociate cell aggregates.
Add 5 mL of ice-cold PBS to the solution.
Centrifuge at 1000 × g for 6 minutes at 4°C.
Discard the supernatant and retain the pellet.
Re-suspend the pellet in 5 mL of ice-cold PBS containing 0.04% BSA by inverting the tube several times.
Pass the solution into a pre-assembled 50 mL Falcon tube topped with a 40 μm cell strainer placed on ice to filter out tissue debris.
Pre-wet the filter with the PBS used for the cells if needed.
Centrifuge at 1000 × g for 6 minutes at 4°C.
Discard the supernatant after centrifugation.
Resuspend the cells in 3 mL of ice-cold PBS containing 0.04% BSA.
Count the cells using a Neubauer counting chamber.
Proceed immediately to step 28-29 for single-cell sequencing to avoid loss of cell viability.
Take 10 μL of cell suspension and mix thoroughly with 10 μL of trypan blue.
Load 10 μL onto the Neubauer chamber to determine the cell viability.
Centrifuge at 1000 × g for 6 min at 4°C, discard the supernatant.
Re-suspend the cell pellet in ice-cold PBS containing 0.04% BSA to obtain a concentration of 700 to 1200 cells/μL.
Proceed immediately to the 10× Genomics protocol for single library preparation and sequencing after cell counting.
Perform single-cell partition into nanolitre-scale Gel-Bead-In-Emulsions (GEMs).
Conduct reverse transcription using Single-Cell 3′ Reagent Kit v2.
Construct libraries for Illumina sequencing.
Load approximately 13,000 cells per sample onto the 10× Genomics Chromium Controller chip.
Perform reverse transcription of single-cell GEMs to produce barcoded cDNA.
Amplify the cDNA using a SimpliAmp Thermal Cycler or similar Thermal Cycler.
Quantify the cDNA library and check the quality using a Bioanalyzer with a High Sensitivity DNA kit.
Sequence in paired-end mode with S1 100-cycles kit using Novaseq 6000 sequencer.
